A E T E R N A T I F

An art archive by Latif

A quiet collection of faces, fragments, flowers and studies — gathered as a record of looking, feeling, and continuing to draw.

01 — Featured exhibition

The first
three.

Three works placed first — the clearest entrance into the artist's visual world. Each one carries a different memory of learning to look.

Graphite on paper01 / 03
01 — TIMELESS BEAUTY

Timeless
Beauty

I wanted to preserve a feeling, not just a face. I drew her at a time when I was falling in love. Every stroke was made with care, carrying a little of what I felt but could not put into words.

Perhaps that is what “timeless beauty in my art” means to me — not that a moment never changes, but that something I once felt can remain alive within a drawing.

Graphite on paper02 / 03
02 — WHERE IDEALS SINK

Where
Ideals Sink

I began to understand that art was never only about pencil and paper. It was about what could pass through them.

This work was born from hope — the kind that makes us look beyond what is in front of us, and sometimes so deeply into our ideals that we forget where the surface ends. I imagined a woman slowly sinking into a world shaped by her own ideals. Yet even beneath the water, her eyes remain open, still searching, still hoping.

Graphite on paper · early study03 / 03
03 — THOSE AYE

Those
Aye

This was one of the first works in which I felt that my ability to shade had truly begun to grow. It was not perfect. I could still see the mistakes, the parts I had yet to understand.

I have always believed that the eyes can reveal what words cannot. Through this work, I began to trust my own ability. And that confidence became the beginning of something more.

04 — Artist

The one
who keeps
looking.

I draw to remember what I might otherwise lose — a face, a feeling, a fragment of a day. These pages are not simply finished works. They are traces of attention.

— the artist, behind AETERNATIF
